top_categories.workout_context: 331 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
29,035ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
At Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 331 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
29,035ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 331 miles.
331 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 29,035ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work supports 29,035ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: October in Northern Vietnam (Hanoi to Ha Giang). Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 331 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 331 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Velo Vietnam Northern Frontier rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, VO2max, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 331 miles of mixed terrain in Northern Vietnam (Hanoi to Ha Giang).
